text:
Simon Nemec is Calgary's newest big minute-eater, and he's still waiting for his first goal as a Flame. The second pick in 2022, acquired from New Jersey, is playing 21 minutes a night, and that role grew when Kevin Bahl got hurt (Sportsnet put the spotlight on him the same week). Seven points in 20 games, all assists.

The goalless run is luck more than anything. He's had 2.8 expected goals and turned none into goals, and the Flames have scored 5.2 fewer goals than their chances with him on. Defensemen at his shot rate usually convert around 6 or 7%. That swings back.

The harder part is the five-on-five play: Calgary is at 46% of the expected goals with him, a bit worse than without him. He's 22 and getting tough minutes on a new team. The tools are there in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season: he stopped 18% of the entries aimed at him (typical is 11%) and carried the puck in on 48% of his entries. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.0 wins above replacement in New Jersey, mostly from offense. Watch the first goal; it tends to loosen a young player up.
